progression.prerequisiteKnowledge: C1 to C8 (including C6a and C6b) and Year 11: K expressions with powers and without solids and water (C5); the three calculation types and ICE tables with the measured value in the Equilibrium row first (C6a); Q and the Q against K rule (C8); mole ratios, c = n / V and powers.
progression.startsWith: What a calculation question gives and what it asks, and how that decides the method.
progression.stopsAfter: Finding K from settled amounts; finding K from a start plus one settled value with an ICE table; deciding a direction from Q against K with a solid present; saying why the same numbers are K only for an equilibrium mixture. No x, shortcuts or amount added (G03b).
progression.nextLesson: G03b: every type of HSC equilibrium calculation, part 2: find concentrations and the amount added.

teaching.task: Pick the method for an unseen equilibrium calculation that gives concentrations or amounts, find K or compare Q with K, and avoid the classic slip for that type.
teaching.causalExplanation: What a question gives and what it asks decide the method. K is a ratio of concentrations, so amounts in a vessel are divided by its volume first, and coefficients are powers. The measured value goes in the Equilibrium row, its change is equilibrium minus initial and the coefficients set the other changes; only equilibrium values go into K. Q has the form of K with the current concentrations, and Q below K means too little product, so the forward reaction wins. The same ratio is K only when the mixture is at equilibrium; for any other mixture it is Q, compared with K.
teaching.conversationalApproach: Opens with the five-card board and lights the three types of part one, takes types one, two and four in short segments with one example and one named slip each, including a pause-and-answer on direction with a solid, then tests the K or Q decision on the first vessel numbers at another temperature, and closes with the decision board and a handoff to part two.
teaching.openingDecision: A calculation gives you some concentrations or amounts. Do you find K, build an ICE table, or work out Q?
teaching.understandingCheck: For 2SO2 + O2 = 2SO3 with K = 229 at this temperature, a vessel holds [SO2] = 0.150, [O2] = 0.0750 and [SO3] = 0.300 mol/L: which way will it run?
teaching.curriculumScope: Calculate equilibrium constants from supplied data and use the reaction quotient to predict direction (Module 5). Every question is written for HSCScience and is not presented as an official question. Concentrations from K, amount-added problems (G03b), marks allocation, temperature dependence of K, Ksp and acid calculations are deferred.

design.visualSystem: Explainer engine: warm paper stage, handwritten Caveat headings, amber doodle layer, the C6a type cards extended to five with lit and dim states, the C6 ICE table with the equilibrium-row-first pen arrow and E minus I bracket, the C5 expression builder, the C8 log number line and small coded vessel vignettes. Colour key as C2 to C8: forward blue, reverse amber, equal teal, made plus green, used up minus red.
design.transitionPlan: The five-card board sets the lesson and returns at the end; each type gets a fresh board in the same three zones; the scene 2 concentrations stay as a small thumbnail and the scene 3 K as a teal card for the attempt; the log number line returns for Q; the feedback rebuilds the scene 2 line and relabels it; scene crossfade with settle.
